title: PAIN-LESS: Postoperative Acupuncture In Lumbar Elective Spine Surgery – a single center randomized controlled trial
summary:
Background: After surgery on the lower spine for a slipped disc or narrowing of the spinal canal, many people have severe pain in the first days. Some still have limitations in daily life months later. Acupuncture, the insertion of fine needles at specific points of the body and the ear, is widely used for back pain, but it has hardly been studied directly after this kind of surgery.
Research question: Does a short course of acupuncture in the first two days after surgery improve daily functioning three months later?
Methods: 162 patients are randomly assigned to three groups. All receive the hospital's usual pain treatment. The first group additionally receives real acupuncture, the second a simulated acupuncture with very shallow needles at places that are not acupuncture points. The third group receives no additional treatment. Patients in the two acupuncture groups do not know which form they receive. Treatment consists of four 20-minute sessions on the first and second day after surgery. Questionnaires over three months record limitations in daily life, pain intensity, use of painkillers and satisfaction.
conditions: Postoperative pain and disability after elective lumbar decompression surgery for degenerative disease
Lumbar and other intervertebral disc disorders with radiculopathy

Standard care alone: standardised perioperative pain management according to the institutional SOP (basic analgesia with paracetamol and NSAID or metamizole, gabapentinoid, intraoperative local anaesthetic wound infiltration, oxycodone as rescue medication) without additional intervention.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Scheduled elective lumbar sequestrectomy or elective osteoligamentous decompression for degenerative disease, including revision surgery for the same indication
- Capacity to consent and written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Acupuncture treatment within the previous 3 months
- Marked skin lesions or similar at the acupuncture sites
- Severe psychiatric disorder or dementia
- Pregnancy or breastfeeding
- Haemophilia A or B, or platelet count below 100,000/µl
- Spinal infection (abscess, spondylodiscitis)
- Kyphoplasty, trauma surgery, oncological lumbar surgery, or fusion/instrumentation
- Intolerance of silicone or stainless steel
